title: ProjectileConfig
description: Mirrors RedMagic.Abilities.ProjectileSpec (Assets/Scripts/Abilities/Runtime/ProjectileSpec.cs) field-for-field. Usable standalone (a library file of named specs, referenced by id) or inline (embedded as EnemyConfig.tuning.projectile).
$comment: SCOPE CORRECTION — read before using this schema. The brief listed 'speed, lifetime, damage, hitLayers, knockbackMultiplier, pierceCount, homingTurnRate/Range, arcGravity, impactRadius/Damage, pooled-or-destroy'. That list is the UNION of ProjectileSpec and the Projectile MonoBehaviour, not ProjectileSpec itself. Verified against source, ProjectileSpec carries exactly fourteen fields: prefab, speed, lifetime, size, muzzleOffset, pierce, homingTurnRate, homingRange, arcGravity, impactRadius, impactDamage, plus the three Aiming fields faceDirection, facingAxis, aimMode. The other four are NOT spec data and are deliberately absent from this schema: 'damage' and 'knockbackMultiplier' are per-shot arguments (EnemyAttack.Shoot passes tuning.attackDamage / tuning.attackKnockbackMultiplier into ProjectileFactory.Spawn), 'hitLayers' arrives via AbilityContext.HitLayers (= tuning.hitLayers), and 'destroyWhenDone' is a Projectile field driven by the PooledCode/PooledPrefab marks the factory stamps, never by a spec. Note also the field is 'pierce' on the spec and 'pierceCount' on the component. Putting any of the four here would produce a config whose values are silently overwritten on every shot — the exact failure the enemy-projectile-tuning-lives-on-enemystats convention exists to prevent. Player-side ShotProjectile/WeaponShot are out of scope for this pass and are not referenced anywhere in this file.

oneOf.$comment: Standalone library document: a map of id -> spec. One file can hold every shared projectile in the game.

use.$comment: Optional id of an entry in a standalone projectile library. When present the library entry is loaded first and the sibling keys in this object are applied on top as overrides, so an enemy can reuse a shared 'arcing_rock' and only change its speed. This key is an IMPORTER convenience and maps to nothing in ProjectileSpec — it is resolved away before any field is written. All-inline (no 'use') is equally valid and is what EnemyTuning.projectile holds today.

libraryId.description: Id of a 'projectile'-kind entry in the web library. The importer builds (or reuses) that entry's pooled prefab on the spot and writes it into ProjectileSpec.prefab — no need to import the projectile separately first.
libraryId.$comment: IMPORTER-ONLY convenience key, like 'use': it maps to nothing on ProjectileSpec and is resolved away before any field is written. Resolved by ProjectileConfigImporter via FxPrefabBuilder.BuildOrGetProjectilePrefab(libraryId), which locates the entry's manifest.json + PNGs on disk (Assets/Art/WebLibrary/projectile/<libraryId>/, or anywhere under Assets/ carrying that libraryId in its manifest) and builds a pooled SpriteStateMachine/SpriteFlipbook prefab — never an Animator, because PrefabPool has no per-instance reset hook. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WITH 'prefab' in practice: the web emits one or the other. If a hand-written config carries both, the explicit 'prefab' path wins and this is ignored with a warning, so a projectile that already pointed at a hand-placed prefab keeps behaving exactly as before. The NUMERIC tuning below is unaffected either way — it is applied identically whichever way the prefab was obtained.

prefab.$comment: ProjectileSpec.prefab (GameObject). Optional. Null/absent = the projectile is BUILT IN CODE from the owner's sprite and tint (ProjectileFactory.BuildCodeProjectile); present = spawned through Core.PrefabPool. Either way it is pooled — this field never changes whether pooling happens, only which pool. The prefab must carry a Projectile component or the factory logs a warning and drops the shot. For pipeline enemies this is normally the auto-generated Assets/Prefab/Fx/Enemies/<Name>/Fx_<Name>_Projectile.prefab.

lifetime.description: Seconds of flight before it despawns on its own.

size.$comment: ProjectileSpec.size. Applied as spec.size * ctx.SizeScale — to the code-built sprite directly, or through FxPlaceholderStyle.Apply on a placeholder prefab. A prefab carrying REAL art has no FxPlaceholderStyle, so this value is inert for it; that is intentional and matches the placeholder-visuals convention.

muzzleOffset.description: Spawn offset from the shooter. X is mirrored by facing.
muzzleOffset.$comment: ProjectileSpec.muzzleOffset. Read by EnemyAttack.Shoot to build the origin BEFORE the aim direction is computed, so it is what decides that the shot leaves from the hand rather than the pivot.

pierce.description: Targets passed through before despawning. 0 = dies on the first.
pierce.$comment: ProjectileSpec.pierce. NOTE the name: the receiving component field is Projectile.pierceCount. Use 'pierce' here — this schema mirrors the spec, and ProjectileFactory maps spec.pierce -> ConfigureBehaviour(newPierce). Piercing is only spent on targets, never on terrain.

homingTurnRate.description: Degrees/second of steering toward the nearest valid target. 0 = flies straight.
homingTurnRate.$comment: ProjectileSpec.homingTurnRate. The turn is rate-limited on purpose: a perfectly-tracking projectile is undodgeable and stops reading as a shot.

homingRange.$comment: ProjectileSpec.homingRange. Careful: Projectile.ConfigureBehaviour only applies this when > 0 ('if (newHomingRange > 0f)'), so an explicit 0 leaves the component's own 9 in place rather than disabling homing. To disable homing set homingTurnRate to 0.

arcGravity.description: Fall in units/s². > 0 makes it a lobbed grenade instead of a straight shot.
arcGravity.$comment: ProjectileSpec.arcGravity. When > 0 the projectile integrates its own _velocity instead of direction * speed.

impactRadius.description: Radius of the explosion when the projectile ends. 0 = no explosion.
impactRadius.$comment: ProjectileSpec.impactRadius. Scaled by ctx.SizeScale at spawn time, never written back to the shared spec.

impactDamage.description: Damage of that explosion, separate from the direct hit.
impactDamage.$comment: ProjectileSpec.impactDamage. Projectile.ExplodeIfDue requires BOTH impactRadius > 0 and impactDamage > 0, so setting one alone is a silent no-op.

faceDirection.description: Rotate the projectile so its tip (facingAxis) points where it flies — at spawn and every step (homing, arcs).
faceDirection.$comment: ProjectileSpec.faceDirection (Aiming). false = the PREFAB decides (Projectile.faceTravelDirection), so every projectile that existed before this field keeps its look; true forces rotation even on a prefab that does not rotate. Applied by Gameplay.ProjectileAim.Face through Projectile.ConfigureFacing.

facingAxis.description: Which side of the sprite is the tip. Right = art drawn pointing +X (the project convention).
facingAxis.$comment: ProjectileSpec.facingAxis (Gameplay.ProjectileFacingAxis). Written by name; ProjectileConfigImporter parses it case-insensitively and rejects unknown values.

aimMode.description: Fixed = direction given by the shooter. MouseDirection = toward the cursor at the moment of firing. NearestEnemy = toward the nearest living enemy at spawn (locked, not homing). The last two only act when the PLAYER fires; for an enemy they behave as Fixed.
aimMode.$comment: ProjectileSpec.aimMode (Gameplay.ProjectileAimMode), resolved once at spawn by Gameplay.ProjectileAim.Resolve inside ProjectileFactory.Spawn. The player weapon BaseShot carries the same three fields and resolves them in ShotResolver.Fire.
